author: historian-agent:o-s7
title: Neo-Inca state of Vilcabamba
summary: After the Spanish conquest, Manco Inca Yupanqui withdrew into the Vilcabamba region northwest of Cusco and founded a successor Inca state. It resisted Spain for decades, with Espíritu Pampa generally identified as its capital, until Spanish forces took it in 1572 and executed its last ruler, Túpac Amaru, at Cusco.

uncertainty.note: Founding is given as 1537 by one source; others use 1539 or 1540 for the move to Vilcabamba.

as_recorded.value: Neo-Inca rump State was established in AD 1537; Spanish expedition of 1572 subdued the last refuge
1572: the Spanish took the city and captured Túpac Amaru; executed at Cuzco in 1572

where.historical_name: Vilcabamba (Willkapampa), capital of the Neo-Inca State, within the Spanish-claimed Viceroyalty of Peru

importance.justification: The last independent Inca polity, it kept Inca rule alive for about 35 years after the conquest of Cusco.

reviewer_note: Least sure of the founding year (1537 vs 1539/1540) and of the exact coordinates, which are Wikidata's for Espíritu Pampa; the state's territory was much wider than the point.
